text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Foods and detergent group Unilever sells its four chemicals units to Britain's ICI for 16 bn guilders. (p1)
- Royal Dutch/Shell's refinery in Pernis is working on a plan to inject carbon dioxide into the ground. (p1)
- ABN Amro bank's prospectus of its flotation on Wall Street divulges new details. (p1)
- PM Wim Kok is not amused about the way proposed tax reforms were "leaked" by junior finance minister Wim Vermeend. (p1)
- Dutch federation of information technology firms Fenit accuses the economic affairs ministry of doing too little for innovative information technology. (p1)
- Music and film company PolyGram gets a 50 million sterling loan from European Investment Bank. (p3)
- Trading company in steel pipes Van Leeuwen Buizen is to buy M & N Valves of the U.S. (p3) VOLKSKRANT
- Council of State's most important adviser condemns decision making in relation to extension of Maastricht Airport. (p1)
- R. Kingsma, board chariman of medical instruments maker Delft Instruments, is to resign at the end of this year. (p2)
- Philips Electronics' U.S. unit Navigation Technologies may stay a loss-maker for a while. (p2)
- Options schemes bring retailer Ahold's top 200 managers some 66 million guilders. (p17) DE TELEGRAAF
- European banks raise the alarm for large number of high quality fake dollars. (p1)
- Employers' association VNO-NCW disappointed with cabinet's withdrawal of bill on working below minimum wages. (p4)
- Province of North Holland is fiercely opposed to a possible referendum on digging a new basin in port of Amsterdam. (p8)
- Thailand's telephone producer Alphatel chooses the Netherlands for its sales and marketing activities in Europe, Middle East, Africa and the U.S. (p35) ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Software producers are to crack down on companies using illegal software. (p1)
- Government leaves decision on privatisation of Schiphol Airport to the next cabinet. (p17) TROUW
- Builder HBG's recent acquisition Wayss & Freytag performed worse in 1996 than originally reported. (p6)
- PIN card payments are still gaining ground despite media offensive to promote electronic purse "the chipknip". (p7)
